understanding: Audit runs are admitted by the driver: Request-AuditLaunchAdmission in driver/10-maintenance.ps1 writes a 'started' (or 'denied') line to audit/audit.launches.jsonl using the DRIVER's $PID, then Start-AuditIfDue launches a SEPARATE detached process, tools/audit-runner.ps1, which waits for idle and calls Invoke-BridgeAudit. The runner writes nothing back to the ledger today, so a 'started' line has no terminal counterpart — the run's outcome (success, partial, idle-skip, error, or death) vanishes. That is the documented root cause of audits not completing since 2026-06-05 (Atom 1.1 of the operator-approved plan dec-20260619-163403-b4ee4c). The fix: keep audit.launches.jsonl, and ADD terminal entries (completed_ok / completed_partial / skipped_not_idle / failed / runner_timeout) carrying pid, channel, report path, runtime, and exit reason, so every admitted run has a durable terminal record. Confirmed from source: Invoke-BridgeAudit returns {status='ok'|'partial', report_json, runtime_sec,...} on completion and {status='locked',pid} when another audit holds the lock; Wait-BridgeIdle returns $true/$false; Get-AuditLaunchAttemptCount counts only decision=='started'; and the named test test-audit-launch-guard.ps1 dot-sources only 10-maintenance.ps1.
summary: Mint a correlation run_id at admission time and thread it driver->runner so a 'started' line and its terminal line can be joined (their pids differ — driver vs runner). Extend the existing single writer Write-AuditLaunchLedgerEntry with optional terminal fields (run_id, report_path, runtime_sec, exit_reason) defaulting to empty/0 so 'started'/'denied' lines stay byte-compatible and the storm guard (which filters decision=='started') is unaffected. Have audit-runner.ps1 classify its own outcome from data it already holds — Wait-BridgeIdle false => skipped_not_idle; Invoke-BridgeAudit status ok/partial/locked; catch => failed — and write EXACTLY ONE terminal line (pid=runner $PID, channel, report path, runtime, sanitized single-line exit reason). Add launch-guard test cases for started->completed_ok, skipped_not_idle, and failed, asserting matching run_id and that terminal lines never increment the attempt count. runner_timeout is defined and schema-supported here but is emitted by the supervisor/reconciler (Atom 1.2), since a killed runner cannot self-report; this atom honestly closes only the graceful-exit and caught-error disappearance, leaving silent death (kill/reboot/hang) to 1.2.

decision_atoms.statement: Introduce a run_id (GUID) generated in Request-AuditLaunchAdmission, written into the 'started' entry, returned to Start-AuditIfDue, and passed to the runner via a new -RunId parameter; every terminal entry echoes the same run_id.
decision_atoms.reason: The 'started' entry is written by the driver process while the terminal entry is written by the separate detached runner — their $PID values differ, so pid alone cannot satisfy the acceptance criterion 'started->completed_ok for that specific run'. A run_id is the only reliable join key, and it also lets reconciliation (Atom 1.2) match dead 'started' lines to missing terminals.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds one parameter and one field plus a small amount of plumbing through three call sites; slightly more surface than a pid-only scheme that would, however, be unreliable.

decision_atoms.statement: Make audit-runner.ps1 the writer of its own terminal state, classifying from data it already has: Wait-BridgeIdle==$false => skipped_not_idle; Invoke-BridgeAudit returns status 'ok' => completed_ok, 'partial' => completed_partial, 'locked' => skipped (audit_lock_held); a thrown exception in the catch => failed; report path from result.report_json and runtime from a stopwatch.
decision_atoms.reason: Only the runner knows the real outcome, the produced report path, and the wall-clock runtime; the driver only sees an opaque detached process. The audit return contract was verified in tools/audit.ps1 (status/report_json/runtime_sec and the locked shape).
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires capturing Invoke-BridgeAudit's return value (currently piped to Out-Null) and handling the 'locked' branch explicitly, rather than the simpler exit-code-only signalling the driver could observe.

decision_atoms.statement: Extend the existing Write-AuditLaunchLedgerEntry with optional terminal fields (RunId, ReportPath, RuntimeSeconds, ExitReason) defaulting to empty/0 — do NOT fork the format or rewrite the file; terminal entries use new decision values only.
decision_atoms.reason: Constraint requires preserving audit.launches.jsonl. Heterogeneous extra fields are valid JSONL, existing readers access by property name, and because Get-AuditLaunchAttemptCount filters decision=='started', terminal lines cannot inflate the per-window attempt count or trigger false max_attempts_per_window storms.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Lines become non-uniform (terminal lines have more fields than started/denied); acceptable for append-only JSONL and cheaper than versioning the schema.

decision_atoms.statement: Keep the canonical, testable terminal writer in driver/10-maintenance.ps1 (so the named test can call it directly) and have the runner reuse the identical schema; pin the runner's field set with a source-regex assertion in the launch-guard test, mirroring the existing 'FileMode::CreateNew' source check.
decision_atoms.reason: test-audit-launch-guard.ps1 dot-sources only 10-maintenance.ps1, so the function the acceptance test exercises must live there. The strict 3-file scope rules out a new shared lib, so the runner either reuses the function or carries a minimal mirror; a source-regex guard catches schema drift cheaply and in the existing test idiom.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: If the runner mirrors the writer instead of dot-sourcing it, there is drift risk (mitigated by the regex pin); if the runner dot-sources 10-maintenance.ps1 instead, it imports control-plane side effects into the detached worker, a larger blast radius. I recommend the minimal mirror + regex pin as lowest runtime risk.

decision_atoms.statement: Guarantee exactly one terminal entry per run via a $terminalWritten flag (primary writes in the try ok/partial/skip and in the catch failed), a finally fallback that writes failed/unknown_exit if none was written, and routing the existing 'tools/audit.ps1 missing -> exit 2' early-return through the same single write point instead of a bare exit.
decision_atoms.reason: Run truth is corrupted both by missing terminals (the original bug) and by duplicate terminals (would double-count outcomes). A single idempotent write point covers every exit path the runner controls.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires a small restructure of the runner's try/catch/finally and replacing bare exits with reason-setting; marginally more code for correctness.

decision_atoms.statement: Define and schema-support runner_timeout in this atom, but emit it from the supervisor/reconciler (Atom 1.2), not the runner; state plainly that Atom 1.1 closes graceful-exit and caught-error disappearance only, while silent death (external kill, reboot, hard hang) is closed by 1.2's dead-'started' TTL reconciliation.
decision_atoms.reason: A killed or hung runner cannot write its own terminal line, and Atom 1.1's acceptance does not test runner_timeout. Carrying the decision value and fields now keeps 1.2 a thin follow-up and avoids over-scoping an 'atomic, commit-in-minutes' change.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Atom 1.1 is therefore a partial fix for 'runs disappear without a trace' — the most dangerous case (silent process death) still needs 1.2; honesty here prevents a false sense of completeness.

assumptions: Invoke-BridgeAudit's return contract is stable: {status='ok'|'partial', report_json, report_md, runtime_sec, ...} on completion and {status='locked', pid} when the audit lock is held (verified in tools/audit.ps1 lines ~1621 and ~1879-1885).
Wait-BridgeIdle returns a [bool] ($true idle / $false timeout), per its header comment.

PowerShell finally blocks run on normal completion and on caught exceptions, but NOT on external process kill — so the finally fallback covers controlled exits, and uncovered silent death is explicitly delegated to Atom 1.2.

tools/test-audit-launch-guard.ps1 is the acceptance harness for this atom and may be extended with synthetic terminal-write cases (it already constructs a temp audit dir and exercises Request-AuditLaunchAdmission directly).
No new config keys are required; existing audit.* settings suffice and run_id is an internal correlation token.
Adding extra fields to terminal JSONL lines does not break any consumer of audit.launches.jsonl (all observed consumers read by property name and filter by decision).
The terminal entry's pid should be the runner's $PID (the real worker, registered as Register-ChildProcess label 'audit'); the 'started' entry keeps the driver pid, with run_id joining the two.

risks.risk: Schema drift between a runner-side mirror writer and the canonical writer in 10-maintenance.ps1, producing terminal lines the readers/tests don't expect.
risks.mitigation: Prefer reusing the single canonical writer; if mirroring, keep an identical ordered-hashtable field list and pin it with a source-regex assertion in the launch-guard test (same idiom as the existing CreateNew check).

risks.risk: Dot-sourcing driver/10-maintenance.ps1 into the detached runner to reuse the writer pulls in control-plane top-level code and $bridgeRoot/$script: dependencies, potentially breaking the audit worker entirely.
risks.mitigation: Favor the minimal inline mirror in the runner over dot-sourcing the control-plane file; if dot-sourcing is chosen, set $bridgeRoot first, wrap in try/catch, and prove driver.ps1 -SelfTest + smoke.ps1 still pass.

risks.risk: A terminal entry accidentally written with decision=='started' (or a change to Get-AuditLaunchAttemptCount) would inflate the per-window count and cause false max_attempts_per_window denials — a launch-starvation regression on control-plane code.
risks.mitigation: Use only distinct terminal decision values; leave Get-AuditLaunchAttemptCount's decision=='started' filter untouched; add a test asserting that writing terminal entries does not change the admitted attempt count.

risks.risk: Exception messages used as exit_reason can contain newlines, and ConvertTo-AuditLaunchJsonLine throws on any CR/LF (it enforces single-line JSONL), so a 'failed' write could itself throw and again leave no terminal trace.
risks.mitigation: Sanitize exit_reason before writing — collapse all whitespace/newlines to single spaces and truncate to a bounded length; wrap the terminal write in try/catch with a last-resort plain-text fallback to audit.log so failure to record is itself logged.

risks.risk: Double or missing terminal entries across the try/catch/finally and early-exit paths corrupt run truth.
risks.mitigation: Single $terminalWritten guard, one write point reached by every controlled exit (including the audit-missing path), and a finally fallback for unanticipated exits.

risks.risk: Misclassifying the status=='locked' return as completed_ok (no report was produced) would falsely mark a non-run as a success.
risks.mitigation: Branch on 'locked' explicitly and record it as a skip (exit_reason 'audit_lock_held') with no report path, distinct from completed_ok.

minimal_version: 1) driver/10-maintenance.ps1: extend Write-AuditLaunchLedgerEntry with optional -RunId/-ReportPath/-RuntimeSeconds/-ExitReason (defaults empty/0, existing started/denied calls unchanged); have Request-AuditLaunchAdmission mint a run_id, include it in the 'started' entry, and return it; thread -RunId from Start-AuditIfDue into the runner's argument list. 2) tools/audit-runner.ps1: accept -RunId, start a stopwatch on entry, capture Wait-BridgeIdle and the Invoke-BridgeAudit return value, classify (idle false=>skipped_not_idle; ok=>completed_ok; partial=>completed_partial; locked=>skipped/audit_lock_held; catch=>failed), and write EXACTLY ONE terminal line (pid=runner $PID, channel, report_path from result.report_json, runtime_sec, sanitized single-line exit_reason) via the canonical writer/mirror, with a $terminalWritten guard, a finally fallback, and the audit-missing early-exit routed through the same write point. 3) tools/test-audit-launch-guard.ps1: add synthetic cases proving started->completed_ok (matching run_id; pid/channel/runtime/exit_reason present), skipped_not_idle, and failed, plus an assertion that terminal lines do not increment Get-AuditLaunchAttemptCount; if the runner mirrors the writer, add a source-regex schema-parity check on audit-runner.ps1. Checks: [Parser]::ParseFile on all three .ps1 (zero errors), run tools/test-audit-launch-guard.ps1 green, driver.ps1 -SelfTest, smoke.ps1.
advanced_version: On top of the minimal version: (a) Extract the launch-ledger helpers (ConvertTo/From-AuditLaunchJsonLine, Write-AuditLaunchLedgerEntry incl. terminal, Get-AuditLaunchAttemptCount) into a small shared lib/audit-launch-ledger.ps1 dot-sourced by driver, runner, and test — a single source of truth that eliminates mirror drift entirely (deferred from the atomic change because it adds a 4th file). (b) Wire runner_timeout emission into the driver's child-process supervision (the path that kills a hung 'audit' child) and into Atom 1.2's dead-'started' TTL reconciliation so silent process death finally gets a terminal record, closing the original root cause completely. (c) Maintain an audit.last_run.json snapshot of the most recent terminal state (decision, run_id, runtime, report path, exit reason) so the auditor freshness alert (Atom 1.3) and operators can read current run truth without scanning the whole JSONL. (d) Add a runtime human-readable 'runtime' string alongside numeric runtime_sec to match the contract's duration-string wording while keeping a machine-joinable field.
